investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exhausted (limit=100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval environment has hit the maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents, preventing the observability check from provisioning a test agent and collecting required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 concurrent agents. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T05:29:23Z), that cap was already reached, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 with "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval check cannot create a new agent, it cannot satisfy any assertion in the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]), and all downstream sibling checks that depend on a freshly created agent also fail with the identical error. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion condition; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure originates at agent creation before any downstream step executes.
Evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, meaning no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever collected — consistent with creation being blocked before any VM was provisioned.
Latency for all three failing calls is low (1506 ms, 1090 ms, 1216 ms), indicating the 409 was returned immediately by the swarm API without any VM provisioning attempt.
The error message embeds a nested swarm error: code=conflict, message=conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100, confirming the quota ceiling is exactly 100 agents.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] Eval-environment swarm agent quota is exhausted: a prior eval run or test provisioning cycle created agents that were never cleaned up, leaving the slot count at or above the 100-agent limit and blocking new creation.

[High confidence] Leaked/zombie swarm agents from previous failed eval runs: if the eval teardown step did not delete the agent after a prior failure, agents accumulate over time until the quota is hit.
[Medium confidence] The 100-agent quota is shared between the eval/observability system and real workloads in the same environment, and organic growth of real agents has consumed all available slots.
[Low confidence] The quota limit itself (100) is misconfigured or too low for the current scale of the environment, causing legitimate concurrent demand to exceed it even with proper cleanup.

reproductionSteps.label: Query current swarm agent count to confirm quota saturation
reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?limit=100 (or equivalent list endpoint) and count total active agents
reproductionSteps.details: If the returned count equals or exceeds 100, quota exhaustion is confirmed.

reproductionSteps.label: Filter for agents created by the observability eval system
reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?createdBy=<eval-service-identity> or filter by eval-specific name/tag pattern
reproductionSteps.details: Identify how many of the 100 slots are held by leaked eval agents versus real workloads.

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt to manually POST /api/agents with eval credentials and observe the 409
reproductionSteps.command: POST /api/agents {<minimal eval agent payload>}
reproductionSteps.details: Should reproduce the identical 409 conflict response seen in the eval evidence.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect eval teardown logs around the previous eval run window
reproductionSteps.details: Check whether the cleanup/delete step for the agent created in the prior eval cycle executed successfully or was skipped due to an earlier failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Delete confirmed leaked eval agents and re-run the eval check
reproductionSteps.command: DELETE /api/agents/<agentId> for each identified leaked eval agent, then re-trigger remote-agent-create check
reproductionSteps.details: If the check passes after freeing slots, leaked agents are the confirmed cause.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle assertions, so no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100. At the time the eval ran (2026-06-14T05:29:25–27Z), the quota was already exhausted, causing every POST /api/agents call to return 409 Conflict with code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval harness depends on successfully creating a new agent as its first step, all downstream state-polling and runtime checks were blocked before they could execute, leaving the expectedOutputContract entirely unfulfilled. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no direct evidence of user-traffic impact is present in the supplied data.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned the identical 409 error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the quota ceiling has been reached.
POST /api/agents was the failing call in every check, indicating the agent-creation step is the shared dependency that blocked all downstream eval assertions.
No required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were populated in any check's evidence object, consistent with failure at the very first provisioning step.

Latencies for all three checks (1090 ms, 1506 ms, 1216 ms) are well below the warning threshold (5000 ms) and outage threshold (20000 ms), confirming the 409 was returned quickly — not a timeout or network issue.
All three checks failed within a 2-second window (05:29:25–05:29:27Z), indicating a systemic quota condition rather than a transient per-request error.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's swarm org or account has accumulated 100 agents from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota before this run began.
[Likely] The eval harness lacks a teardown/cleanup step that deletes agents created in prior runs, causing quota to grow monotonically across eval executions.
[Possible] A quota limit of 100 is too low for the volume of eval runs or concurrent environments sharing the same swarm org/account, requiring a quota increase.
[Less likely] A prior eval run crashed mid-execution, leaving orphaned agents that were never deleted, accelerating quota exhaustion.
[Unlikely but possible] The quota limit was recently lowered by a configuration change on the swarm backend, causing previously passing evals to now fail.

reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents (or equivalent swarm list endpoint) and count total active agents for the eval org/account — expect count at or near 100
reproductionSteps.details: Verify the quota is genuinely exhausted by listing all agents in the swarm org used by the eval harness.

reproductionSteps.details: Expect a 409 response with code 'conflict' and message 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if quota is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Identify stale/orphaned eval agents
reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the eval harness (e.g., by name prefix, tag, or creation timestamp) to identify agents that should have been cleaned up.

reproductionSteps.label: Delete stale eval agents to free quota
reproductionSteps.command: DELETE /api/agents/{agentId} for each identified stale eval agent
reproductionSteps.details: Remove enough agents to bring the count below 100, then re-run the eval suite to confirm checks pass.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the full remote-agents eval suite after cleanup
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm that remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all pass and that required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are populated.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T05:29Z with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval cannot provision a new agent to complete its runtime assertion, so no expected-output contract evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is returning "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on POST /api/agents, meaning the production org used by the AURA observability eval has hit the maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents. Because the eval lifecycle depends on successfully creating a fresh agent before it can test VM readiness, lifecycle state, and chat readiness, all downstream checks cascade-fail before any runtime assertion can be evaluated. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates a broader production outage for end users.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The 409 was returned at low latency (1090 ms, 1216 ms, 1506 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-gate rejection rather than a timeout or infrastructure fault.
The expected-output contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message — none were collected because agent creation never succeeded.
The assertion path 'message' containing 'hello from aura' was never reached, confirming the failure is at the creation step, not the runtime response step.
All three checks share the same startedAt window (05:29:25–05:29:27 UTC), indicating a single quota state blocked the entire eval run rather than a transient per-request error.
possibleCauses: (Highest confidence) The org account used by the AURA eval harness has accumulated 100 swarm agents that were not cleaned up from previous eval runs, exhausting the quota and blocking new agent creation.
(High confidence) A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown/cleanup step, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
(Medium confidence) The agent quota limit of 100 is shared between the eval harness org and real workloads in the same org, and organic usage has consumed the remaining capacity.

(Low confidence) The swarm backend's quota enforcement is miscounting active agents (e.g., counting soft-deleted or terminal-state agents), causing a false quota-exceeded response even if fewer than 100 live agents exist.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after emitting a `generation_start` frame because the agent runtime returned a 404, surfaced as `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED`. The harness was unreachable at the configured endpoint, preventing any progress frames or completion artifacts from being produced, so both required evidence fields (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) were never populated.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the eval harness attempted to open a session for image generation. This indicates the harness is either not deployed at the URL resolved from `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, is deployed at a different path or port than expected, or is running an incompatible version whose session-open endpoint no longer exists at the expected route. The failure occurred within 2010 ms (well under the warning threshold of 180 000 ms), confirming this is a hard connectivity/routing failure, not a latency or generation-quality issue. No sibling checks or source hints were supplied, so the exact misconfigured URL or version mismatch cannot be pinpointed from this evidence alone.
proof: failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].event = "generation_error" with code "SESSION_OPEN_FAILED" and message explicitly stating "agent runtime endpoint not found (404)".
failedCheck.message confirms missing required evidence: frameTypes and imageUrlPresent — neither was ever emitted because the stream terminated at session-open.
failedCheck.latencyMs = 2010 ms — the stream aborted in ~2 seconds, consistent with a fast 404 response rather than a timeout or generation failure.

failedCheck.evidence.frames[0] shows generation_start with mode=image was emitted, confirming the eval harness itself initiated the request successfully; the 404 came from the downstream agent runtime, not the eval runner.
failedCheck.evidence.frames[2] is an empty message frame, indicating the stream closed with no further data after the error.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The agent runtime harness is not deployed or is down at the URL currently configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL — the 404 is returned immediately, meaning the HTTP server exists but the specific session-open route is absent or the base URL is wrong.

(Likely) A version mismatch between the eval harness and the agent runtime: the runtime was updated and the session-open endpoint was moved, renamed, or removed, making the previously valid route return 404.
(Possible) The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable is misconfigured in the production eval environment — pointing to a stale, decommissioned, or incorrect host/port/path.

(Less likely) A network-layer change (e.g., ingress rule, reverse-proxy path rewrite, or DNS change) in the production environment is intercepting the request and returning 404 before it reaches the harness process.

reproductionSteps.label: Identify the resolved harness URL from environment configuration
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the production eval environment for the values of LOCAL_HARNESS_URL and SWARM_BASE_URL to determine the exact endpoint being targeted.

reproductionSteps.command: curl -v -X POST "<resolved LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL>/session/open" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"mode":"image"}'
reproductionSteps.details: Replace the URL with the actual configured value. A 404 response confirms the route does not exist at that address.

reproductionSteps.label: Check harness process health at the configured host and port
reproductionSteps.command: curl -v "<resolved LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL>/health"
reproductionSteps.details: If this also returns 404 or connection refused, the harness process is not running or is bound to a different address.

reproductionSteps.label: Verify harness deployment status in the production environment
reproductionSteps.details: Check the deployment system (container orchestrator, process manager, or swarm config) to confirm the harness container/process is running and its exposed port matches the configured URL.

reproductionSteps.label: Compare harness version against eval harness expectations
reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the running harness version (via its version endpoint or deployment manifest) and compare it against the version the eval harness was built to target, looking for breaking route changes.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after emitting a `generation_start` frame because the agent runtime returned a 404, surfaced as `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED`. The harness was unreachable at the configured endpoint, preventing any progress frames or completion artifacts from being produced, so both required evidence fields (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) were never populated.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the eval harness attempted to open a session for image generation. This indicates the harness is either not deployed at the URL resolved from `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, is deployed at a different path or port than expected, or is running an incompatible version whose session-open endpoint no longer exists at the expected route. The failure occurred within 2010 ms (well under the warning threshold of 180 000 ms), confirming this is a hard connectivity/routing failure, not a latency or generation-quality issue. No sibling checks or source hints were supplied, so the exact misconfigured URL or version mismatch cannot be pinpointed from this evidence alone.
proof: failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].event = "generation_error" with code "SESSION_OPEN_FAILED" and message explicitly stating "agent runtime endpoint not found (404)".
failedCheck.message confirms missing required evidence: frameTypes and imageUrlPresent — neither was ever emitted because the stream terminated at session-open.
failedCheck.latencyMs = 2010 ms — the stream aborted in ~2 seconds, consistent with a fast 404 response rather than a timeout or generation failure.

failedCheck.evidence.frames[0] shows generation_start with mode=image was emitted, confirming the eval harness itself initiated the request successfully; the 404 came from the downstream agent runtime, not the eval runner.
failedCheck.evidence.frames[2] is an empty message frame, indicating the stream closed with no further data after the error.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The agent runtime harness is not deployed or is down at the URL currently configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL — the 404 is returned immediately, meaning the HTTP server exists but the specific session-open route is absent or the base URL is wrong.

(Likely) A version mismatch between the eval harness and the agent runtime: the runtime was updated and the session-open endpoint was moved, renamed, or removed, making the previously valid route return 404.
(Possible) The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable is misconfigured in the production eval environment — pointing to a stale, decommissioned, or incorrect host/port/path.

(Less likely) A network-layer change (e.g., ingress rule, reverse-proxy path rewrite, or DNS change) in the production environment is intercepting the request and returning 404 before it reaches the harness process.

reproductionSteps.label: Identify the resolved harness URL from environment configuration
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the production eval environment for the values of LOCAL_HARNESS_URL and SWARM_BASE_URL to determine the exact endpoint being targeted.

reproductionSteps.label: Probe the session-open endpoint directly with curl
reproductionSteps.command: curl -v -X POST "<resolved LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL>/session/open" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"mode":"image"}'
reproductionSteps.details: Replace the URL with the actual configured value. A 404 response confirms the route does not exist at that address.

reproductionSteps.label: Check harness process health at the configured host and port
reproductionSteps.command: curl -v "<resolved LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL>/health"
reproductionSteps.details: If this also returns 404 or connection refused, the harness process is not running or is bound to a different address.

reproductionSteps.label: Verify harness deployment status in the production environment
reproductionSteps.details: Check the deployment system (container orchestrator, process manager, or swarm config) to confirm the harness container/process is running and its exposed port matches the configured URL.

reproductionSteps.label: Compare harness version against eval harness expectations
reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the running harness version (via its version endpoint or deployment manifest) and compare it against the version the eval harness was built to target, looking for breaking route changes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exhausted (limit=100)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval environment has hit the maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents, preventing the observability check from provisioning a test agent and collecting required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 concurrent agents. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T05:29:23Z), that cap was already reached, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 with "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval check cannot create a new agent, it cannot satisfy any assertion in the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]), and all downstream sibling checks that depend on a freshly created agent also fail with the identical error. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion condition; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure originates at agent creation before any downstream step executes.
Evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, meaning no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever collected — consistent with creation being blocked before any VM was provisioned.
Latency for all three failing calls is low (1506 ms, 1090 ms, 1216 ms), indicating the 409 was returned immediately by the swarm API without any VM provisioning attempt.
The error message embeds a nested swarm error: code=conflict, message=conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100, confirming the quota ceiling is exactly 100 agents.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] Eval-environment swarm agent quota is exhausted: a prior eval run or test provisioning cycle created agents that were never cleaned up, leaving the slot count at or above the 100-agent limit and blocking new creation.

[High confidence] Leaked/zombie swarm agents from previous failed eval runs: if the eval teardown step did not delete the agent after a prior failure, agents accumulate over time until the quota is hit.
[Medium confidence] The 100-agent quota is shared between the eval/observability system and real workloads in the same environment, and organic growth of real agents has consumed all available slots.
[Low confidence] The quota limit itself (100) is misconfigured or too low for the current scale of the environment, causing legitimate concurrent demand to exceed it even with proper cleanup.

reproductionSteps.label: Query current swarm agent count to confirm quota saturation
reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?limit=100 (or equivalent list endpoint) and count total active agents
reproductionSteps.details: If the returned count equals or exceeds 100, quota exhaustion is confirmed.

reproductionSteps.label: Filter for agents created by the observability eval system
reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?createdBy=<eval-service-identity> or filter by eval-specific name/tag pattern
reproductionSteps.details: Identify how many of the 100 slots are held by leaked eval agents versus real workloads.

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt to manually POST /api/agents with eval credentials and observe the 409
reproductionSteps.command: POST /api/agents {<minimal eval agent payload>}
reproductionSteps.details: Should reproduce the identical 409 conflict response seen in the eval evidence.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect eval teardown logs around the previous eval run window
reproductionSteps.details: Check whether the cleanup/delete step for the agent created in the prior eval cycle executed successfully or was skipped due to an earlier failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Delete confirmed leaked eval agents and re-run the eval check
reproductionSteps.command: DELETE /api/agents/<agentId> for each identified leaked eval agent, then re-trigger remote-agent-create check
reproductionSteps.details: If the check passes after freeing slots, leaked agents are the confirmed cause.
